canonical_facts.structure: Five staves: Stave 1 Marley's Ghost, Stave 2 The First of the Three Spirits, Stave 3 The Second of the Three Spirits, Stave 4 The Last of the Spirits, Stave 5 The End of It
canonical_facts.marley_death: Died exactly seven years before Christmas Eve of the story (the story's present night)
canonical_facts.fan_death: The text says only 'she died a woman' — cause never stated explicitly; 'giving birth to Fred' is adaptation inference not textual fact
canonical_facts.bob_cratchit_salary: Fifteen shillings a week (stated in text)
canonical_facts.ghost_of_christmas_present_brothers: More than eighteen hundred brothers (one per Christmas since Christ's birth)
canonical_facts.ignorance_and_want_genders: Ignorance is the boy, Want is the girl
canonical_facts.tiny_tim_church_quote: Bob Cratchit tells Scrooge what Tim said on the way home from church — it is a reported speech, not Tim speaking directly in the scene
canonical_facts.stave_4_sequence: Old Joe's thieves scene — then Cratchit mourning Tiny Tim — then Scrooge's grave (Tiny Tim before grave in Stave 4)
canonical_facts.stave_5_bob_raise: Scrooge raises Bob's salary on Boxing Day (the day after Christmas, when Bob arrives late to the office)
canonical_facts.businessmen_nickname: One businessman calls the dead man 'Old Scratch' (slang for the Devil)
canonical_facts.old_joe_thieves: Charwoman, laundress, and undertaker's man — not 'undertaker' himself
canonical_facts.ghost_present_scabbard: Antique scabbard at the spirit's waist — no sword in it, sheath eaten up with rust
canonical_facts.ignorance_and_want_quote: This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want. Beware them both...but most of all beware this boy
canonical_facts.laocooen_quote: Stave 5 — Scrooge makes 'a perfect Laocoon of himself with his stockings'
canonical_facts.i_am_not_the_man: Stave 4 — said at the graveside pleading with the Spirit
canonical_facts.decrease_surplus_population_speaker: Scrooge in Stave 1 to the charity collectors; echoed back by Ghost of Christmas Present in Stave 3 re Tiny Tim
canonical_facts.god_bless_us_every_one_speaker: Tiny Tim — said at the Cratchit Christmas dinner in Stave 3; also the novella's final line

issues.claim: Fan died young giving birth to Fred, Scrooge's nephew. This explains why Scrooge resents Fred — he blames him for Fan's death.
issues.correct: Dickens never states the cause of Fan's death. The text says only 'she died a woman' and had a child. 'Giving birth' is a common adaptation tradition but not in the text. The claim that Scrooge 'blames Fred for Fan's death' is speculative interpretation presented as textual fact.
issues.source: Project Gutenberg Stave 2 full text; multiple scholarly sources confirming Dickens does not specify cause of Fan's death

issues.claim: Scrooge's laundry woman, charwoman, and undertaker sell his stolen possessions to a fence called Old Joe.
issues.correct: The text specifies a charwoman, laundress, and undertaker's *man* (not 'undertaker' — the undertaker's assistant/employee). A minor mislabelling but 'undertaker' could mislead students about the scene's characters.
issues.source: Dickens Stave 4 original text — 'an undertaker's man' is the precise phrase

issues.claim: Fan died young giving birth to Fred. This explains why Scrooge resents Fred — he blames him for Fan's death, the loss of the only person who truly loved him.
issues.correct: Same as AQA L3: Dickens does not state Fan died in childbirth, and there is no textual basis for Scrooge 'blaming' Fred. This inference conflates common stage adaptation with the source text.
issues.source: Project Gutenberg Stave 2; scholarly sources confirm cause of Fan's death is not given

lessons.title: Stave 2: The Ghost of Christmas Past
Stave 3: The Ghost of Christmas Present

issues.location: Cratchit Christmas section — Tiny Tim church speech
issues.claim: Tiny Tim becomes the emotional core of the scene. He sits by the fire with his 'active little crutch' and says, at church: 'I hope the people saw me in the church, because I was a cripple, and it might be pleasant to them to remember upon Christmas Day, who made lame beggars walk and blind men see.'
issues.correct: This speech is not said by Tiny Tim directly in the scene. In the text, Bob Cratchit *tells Scrooge* what Tim said on the way home from church: 'He told me, coming home, that he hoped the people saw him in the church...' It is reported speech delivered by Bob Cratchit to Scrooge during the ghost's visitation — not Tim speaking at church. Presenting it as Tim saying this 'at church' misrepresents the scene structure and speaker attribution.
issues.source: Project Gutenberg Stave 3 full text; SparkNotes quote attribution confirms Bob's reported speech

issues.claim: Useful quotations across the arc: 'Hard and sharp as flint' (the start), 'I am not the man I was' (the turning point), 'as merry as a schoolboy' (the rebirth).
issues.correct: 'I am not the man I was' is spoken in Stave 4 at Scrooge's graveside — it is indeed a turning point moment, so the tagging is not wrong, but calling it 'the turning point' when it occurs in Stave 4 (the fourth of five staves) while Stave 5 is the actual transformation stave may mislead students into thinking this is a Stave 5 quote. The stave attribution is implicit but could be clearer. Minor labelling issue.

issues.location: Section headed 'Tiny Tim's Death' — placed structurally after the 'Stave 5: The Transformation' heading
issues.claim: The 'Tiny Tim's Death' section appears in the lesson after the 'Stave 5: The Transformation' content block, giving the impression Tiny Tim's death is a Stave 5 event.
issues.correct: Tiny Tim's death is shown to Scrooge in Stave 4 (The Last of the Spirits), not Stave 5. In Stave 4, the narrative order is: (1) businessmen discuss the dead man; (2) Old Joe's thieves scene; (3) Cratchit family mourning Tiny Tim; (4) Scrooge's grave. Stave 5 is exclusively about Scrooge's transformed behaviour on Christmas morning and Boxing Day. Placing the Tiny Tim death section under or after the Stave 5 content block is a structural misrepresentation of the novella's chronology that could directly mislead students in exam responses.
issues.source: Project Gutenberg Stave 4 full text; SparkNotes Stave 4 summary; confirmed canonical order

issues.claim: Belle appears only in Stave 2, but her significance extends across the whole novella. She tells young Scrooge: 'Another idol has displaced me … a golden one.' ... Belle's departure is the last chance Scrooge had to change before the supernatural intervention of Stave 1.
issues.correct: The sequence is misstated. Belle's departure is depicted in Stave 2 (as a memory from Scrooge's past). Stave 1 occurs first in narrative time — Marley's Ghost visits Scrooge in Stave 1. The lesson says 'before the supernatural intervention of Stave 1' but the ghost visits happen after Belle's scene (which is a flashback in Stave 2). The intended meaning is probably 'before the spirits intervene in the story's present' but 'before Stave 1' is chronologically incoherent and could confuse students about the stave sequence.
issues.source: Novella structure: Stave 1 is the story's present; Stave 2 contains memories of the past
